lines.japanese: 「うわお！」
lines.english: “Whoa!”

lines.japanese: 人がいないにも関わらず、朝っぱらから芸人じみたリアクションをしてしまいました。
lines.english: Even though no one was around, I reacted like a comedian first thing in the morning.

lines.japanese: なんと下駄箱に、ハートのスタンプで封をされた、可愛らしい封筒が入っていたのです。
lines.english: There, inside my shoe locker, was an adorable envelope with a heart stamped across the seal.

lines.japanese: これはつまり、アレがアレのためにアレするアレっすか。
lines.english: Could this be one of those things where someone does that thing for that reason and you know what happens?

lines.japanese: いわゆるひとつのラブレター。
lines.english: That thing commonly known as a love letter.

lines.japanese: 思わずフッと息を吹きあげて、前髪を揺らしてしまいますよ。
lines.english: I couldn’t help blowing upward with a suave little puff that ruffled my bangs.

lines.japanese: あ、そー。モテるんだねえ、羽田タカシ君は。
lines.english: Oh, I see. Takashi Haneda is popular with the ladies.

lines.japanese: ええ、そうね、そりゃ千歳鷲介君へのアレじゃないでしょうからね。ぜんぜん嬉しかないっすよね。
lines.english: Sure, right. It obviously wasn’t addressed to Shuusuke Chitose. No reason for me to be happy at all.

lines.japanese: はーあ、俺もこんな古典的イベントの起こる、ドッキドキ学園生活を楽しみたかったなあ。
lines.english: Siiigh. I wanted to enjoy a heart-pounding school life where classic events like this actually happened to me.

lines.japanese: 愛しの日和子さんも、昼休みランチや放課後デートぐらいは付きあってくれたけど、ラブレターを下駄箱になんて手の込んだ真似、頼んでもやってくれないだろうなあ──
lines.english: My beloved Hiyoko would join me for lunch or go on a date after school, but even if I begged, I doubted she would go to the trouble of putting a love letter in my shoe locker—

lines.japanese: ──なーんて冗談半分に愚痴りながら封筒をひっくり返してみれば、右隅に差出人らしき名前。
lines.english: —so I was grumbling, half in jest, when I turned the envelope over and found what appeared to be the sender’s name in the right corner.

lines.japanese: 『ひょこ』
lines.english: “Hyoko.”

lines.japanese: ふむ、なんか見覚えのある大雑把な……もとい、個性的で力強い筆跡だな。まるで日和子さんみたい──
lines.english: Hmm. That rough—no, distinctive and vigorous—handwriting looked somehow familiar. Almost exactly like Hiyoko’s—

lines.japanese: いや、みたいっていうか、これはまさに──
lines.english: No, not just like it. This was—

lines.japanese: 本人！？
lines.english: The real deal?!

lines.japanese: 『今日の放課後、屋上で会えませんか？』
lines.english: “Could you meet me on the roof after school today?”

lines.japanese: 授業中にこっそり読んでみたら、手紙には（要約して）そんなようなことが書いてありました。
lines.english: When I secretly read the letter in class, that was more or less what it said, to summarize.

lines.japanese: 放課後、屋上で──
lines.english: After school, on the roof—

lines.japanese: ──まあ、それはよしとして、しかしなぜ突然こんな、手間のかかるアナクロな通信手段で？
lines.english: —well, that part was fine. But why had she suddenly chosen such a laborious, anachronistic means of communication?

lines.japanese: 上級生の教室を頻繁に訪れるのは抵抗あるのかもしれませんが、だったらケータイに、電話かメールの一本でもくれればいいのに。
lines.english: Maybe she felt awkward visiting an upperclassman’s classroom too often, but in that case, she could simply call or email my phone.

lines.japanese: うーん、よほど改まった話でもあるのかしら……。
lines.english: Hmm. Did she have something unusually formal to discuss...?

lines.japanese: はっ！　まさか別れ話！？
lines.english: Gasp! Could she be breaking up with me?!

lines.japanese: いやいや、悪い方に考えるのはよそう。こんなときこそ鷲介スピリッツ。
lines.english: No, no. I shouldn’t assume the worst. Times like this called for the Shuusuke spirit.

lines.japanese: ぬるっと考えよう！
lines.english: Think slippery thoughts!

lines.japanese: うん、そう。これはきっと古き良きラブストーリーを好む日和子さんが、靴箱にラブレターとか、屋上に彼氏を呼びだすとか、そういうシチュエーションに憧れてお茶目しただけの話──
lines.english: Yes, of course. Hiyoko loved good old-fashioned romance stories. She must have playfully decided to recreate one of those situations where a girl puts a love letter in a shoe locker and summons her boyfriend to the roof—

lines.japanese: ──ちょっと無理があるか。
lines.english: —maybe that was a bit of a stretch.

lines.japanese: ま、いいや。どうせ放課後になれば分かることだ。
lines.english: Oh, well. I would find out after school either way.

lines.japanese: 俺は日和子さんとの逢引きを楽しみに、消化試合のような授業×６を乗りきりました。
lines.english: Looking forward to my secret rendezvous with Hiyoko, I made it through six classes that felt like games with nothing left at stake.

lines.japanese: 放課後の屋上。部活動の生徒や、悩める若人や、アウトロー気取りのお兄さんらが……普段なら少なからずいるものなのですが。
lines.english: The roof after school. Club members, troubled youths, and boys pretending to be outlaws... Ordinarily, one could expect to find at least a few of each.

lines.japanese: しかし今日は、いかにも冬らしい寒さのせいか、ベンチに一名ばかり佇んでいるのみでした。
lines.english: But perhaps because the day was cold in the most wintry way, only one person stood by the benches.

lines.japanese: それこそが俺を呼びだした──
lines.english: The very person who had called me here—

lines.japanese: 「あっ」
lines.english: “Ah.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは俺の気配に気付くと、顔を上げました。
lines.english: Hiyoko noticed my presence and raised her head.

lines.japanese: が、何を思ったのか、すぐにまた伏せてしまいました。
lines.english: But for some reason, she immediately lowered it again.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん？」
lines.english: “Hiyoko?”

lines.japanese: 「ごっ、ごめんなさい、いきなり呼び出したりして……」
lines.english: “I-I’m sorry for calling you out here so suddenly...”

lines.japanese: いえいえ全然。俺はにっこり笑顔で答えました。さて問題は、いったいどんな御用件なのかと。
lines.english: Not at all. I answered with a bright smile. The question was what exactly she wanted.

lines.japanese: 「小説のネタにでも詰まりました？　それとも何か話でも？」
lines.english: “Are you stuck on an idea for a novel? Or did you want to talk about something?”

lines.japanese: 「いえっ、その……」
lines.english: “No, um...”
“Well...”

lines.japanese: ごにょごにょと口ごもるばかりで、明確な答えが出てきません。
lines.english: She did nothing but mumble, never producing a clear answer.

lines.japanese: なんでしょう、そんな言いにくいことなのかしら。よし、それなら、いつもの調子で──
lines.english: What could it be? Was it really that difficult to say? Very well, then. I would take my usual approach—

lines.japanese: 「あっ！　それとも日和子さん、学校で二人きりになりたくて、こんな人気のない場所・時間に呼びだしたとか～？」
lines.english: “Oh! Or did you pick a time and place where nobody would be around because you wanted me all to yourself at school?”

lines.japanese: 「はい、そうです。鷲介さんと、い、いちゃいちゃしようと思って」
lines.english: “Yes, that’s right. I wanted to... f-flirt with you, Shuusuke.”

lines.japanese: “って、そんなわけあるかあっ！”
lines.english: Any second now: “Like that would ever happen!”

lines.japanese: “ですよねー！”
lines.english: And I’d answer, “Of course it wouldn’t!”

lines.japanese: よし、これでいつもの日和子さんに戻って、すんなりと──
lines.english: There. Back to the usual Hiyoko, and everything would go smoothly—

lines.japanese: ──来ないな。身構えて待ってるのに、恒例のノリツッコミが来ないぞ。
lines.english: —Nothing. I was braced and waiting, but she never played along and then shot me down like usual.

lines.japanese: 「あ、あれ？　日和子さん、このままではまるで、俺といちゃいちゃしたかったことになってしまいますが……？」
lines.english: “U-um, Hiyoko? If this continues, it’s going to sound as if you genuinely wanted to flirt with me...?”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい、おっしゃる通りです。そのために鷲介さんを呼びだしました」
lines.english: “Y-yes, that’s exactly right. That is why I called you here.”

lines.japanese: マジで！？
lines.english: Seriously?!

lines.japanese: え、なに爆弾発言してるんですかこの子。なんだ、罠か。ドッキリか。ああ、爆発オチか。
lines.english: What kind of bombshell was this girl dropping? Was it a trap? A prank? Ah, perhaps the punch line would be an explosion.

lines.japanese: 羽田班の皆さんでも潜んでるのかと思わず辺りを見回してしまう、幸せに不慣れな俺でした。
lines.english: Unused to happiness as I was, I found myself looking around for the rest of Team Haneda hiding nearby.

lines.japanese: いや、でも、ヤラセや演技で顔面をこんなに赤くできるわけないか。
lines.english: But no staging or performance could turn someone’s face this red.

lines.japanese: じゃあ……本当に……？
lines.english: Then... did she truly...?

lines.japanese: 「え、でもそれなら、何も手紙で呼びださなくても……」
lines.english: “But if that’s what you wanted, you didn’t need to summon me with a letter...”

lines.japanese: 「校内での携帯電話の使用は禁止ですよ」
lines.english: “Using a cell phone on school grounds is forbidden.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、なるほど」
lines.english: “Ah. Of course.”

lines.japanese: なんて日和子さんらしい理由なんでしょう。くすりと笑ってしまいました。
lines.english: The reason was so thoroughly Hiyoko that a soft laugh escaped me.

lines.japanese: 「ごめんなさい、嘘です。ほんとは、鷲介さんに手紙を出してみたかったんです」
lines.english: “I’m sorry. That was a lie. I really wanted to try writing you a letter.”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「鷲介さんが卒業したら、下駄箱へ手紙を入れる機会なんて、もうないかなって……」
lines.english: “After you graduate, I may never have another chance to put a letter in your shoe locker...”

lines.japanese: 自らを抱くように、両腕をぎゅっと握る日和子さん。その仕草はきっと、この寒さを凌ぐせいばかりでもないのでしょう。
lines.english: Hiyoko gripped both her arms, as though embracing herself. Surely the gesture did more than protect her from the cold.

lines.japanese: そしていま、俺の身体もまた、ぶるぶる振動しておりました。寒さの引きおこしたシバリングではありません。感動してきつく抱きしめたい衝動を必死で堪えているのです。
lines.english: My body was trembling too. Not from cold-induced shivering, but from my desperate struggle against the urge to crush her in an emotional embrace.

lines.japanese: あ、べつに堪える必要ないのか。日和子さんの方からいちゃいちゃしたいって言ってくれてるんだから、思う存分ハグしてあげよう。
lines.english: Wait, I didn’t need to resist. Hiyoko herself had said she wanted to flirt, so I could hug her to my heart’s content.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さんっ……！」
lines.english: “Hiyoko...!”

lines.japanese: 「ま、待ってください！」
lines.english: “W-wait!”

lines.japanese: 「あれー」
lines.english: “Huh?”

lines.japanese: 身体をナナメらせて逃げる日和子さん。
lines.english: Hiyoko leaned away to escape me.

lines.japanese: 「あ、もしかしてお話したいだけで、こういうのはよろしくないと……？」
lines.english: “Oh, did you only want to talk? Is this sort of thing unwelcome...?”

lines.japanese: 何故か睨まれました。顔を真っ赤にしながら。
lines.english: For some reason, she glared at me with her face burning red.

lines.japanese: 「ちっ、違うんです。そうじゃなくて、その……ま、まだ心の準備が、とか、人が来たらどうしよう、とか……」
lines.english: “Th-that’s not it. I just... I’m not ready yet, and what if someone comes up here...?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、それもそうっすね」
lines.english: “Ah, good point.”

lines.japanese: どう見ても恋人たちの夕暮れだもんな、この光景。落ちつこう、俺。
lines.english: This did look exactly like two lovers on a rooftop at sunset. Calm down, Shuusuke.

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ夕焼けでも見ながらお話しましょっか。日和子さんと放課後を過ごせるだけで、幸せっすよ俺」
lines.english: “Then shall we talk while we watch the sunset? Just getting to spend time after school with you makes me happy.”

lines.japanese: 「そっ、そんなはっきりと……嬉しいですけど……」
lines.english: “Y-you don’t have to say it so plainly... Though it does make me happy...”

lines.japanese: 「でも、あの……それだけじゃないんです」
lines.english: “But, um... that isn’t all.”

lines.japanese: 「え？　それだけじゃないとは？」
lines.english: “What? What else is there?”

lines.japanese: 「この前、アレキサンダーでみんなに言われたことを思いだすと、私って固すぎるのかなとか……鷲介さんに飽きられたりしないかなって」
lines.english: “When I remember what everyone at Alexander said the other day, I start to wonder if I’m too uptight... or whether you might get bored with me.”

lines.japanese: 「だ、だから今日は学校でも……」
lines.english: “S-so today, even at school...”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんの手が恐る恐る近づいてきました。
lines.english: Hiyoko’s hand timidly approached mine.

lines.japanese: そして俺の指先を彼女の指先がちょこんとつまんでくれました。
lines.english: Then her fingertips gently pinched the very tips of my fingers.

lines.japanese: 「このくらい、なら、いいかなって」
lines.english: “I thought... this much might be all right.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さあああん！
lines.english: Hiyokooooo!

lines.japanese: ちょっ、なんてことしてくれるんですか、かわいすぎるにも程がありますよあなた！
lines.english: Wh-what are you doing to me?! There should be a legal limit on how adorable one person can be!

lines.japanese: こ、殺される……この夕焼けの屋上で、俺は今日、日和子さんに惚れ殺される……。
lines.english: I-I’m going to die... Here on this rooftop at sunset, I’m going to die of love for Hiyoko...

lines.japanese: あわわわわと思わずパニクってしまう俺でしたが、しかし同時に──
lines.english: Aaah! I was thrown into a complete panic. But at the same time—

lines.japanese: ──視界の異変に気付きました。
lines.english: —I noticed a change at the edge of my vision.

lines.japanese: 俺はここへ上がって来る際、階段の照明を落としてきました。
lines.english: I had switched off the stairwell light when I came up here.

lines.japanese: ところが、いまそこに、明かりが灯ったのです。
lines.english: But now that light had come on.

lines.japanese: つまり、どなたか第三者が上がってくるってこと。
lines.english: In other words, a third party was on the way up.

lines.japanese: そんなことになったら、日和子さんが大変に恥ずかしい思いをしてしまうでしょう──
lines.english: If that happened, Hiyoko would be deeply embarrassed—

lines.japanese: ──というのは建前で、ふたりきりの甘い時間を邪魔されたくないってのが本音だったり。
lines.english: —which was my official reason. The truth was that I did not want anyone interrupting our sweet time alone.

lines.japanese: 「日和子さん」
lines.english: “Hiyoko.”

lines.japanese: 「は、はい」
lines.english: “Y-yes?”

lines.japanese: 「こっち」
lines.english: “This way.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ……ええっ？」
lines.english: “Wha... What?”

lines.japanese: 俺は日和子さんの手を握って立ちあがりました。
lines.english: I took Hiyoko’s hand and rose to my feet.

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あのっ！　そんな、いきなりっ……！」
lines.english: “What? Um! S-so suddenly...!”

lines.japanese: 「違います、ひとが来そうなんです」
lines.english: “That’s not it. I think someone’s coming.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ！」
lines.english: “What?!”

lines.japanese: ただならぬ勢いに呑まれる日和子さん。冷静に考えれば、今はたまたま二人きりだったというだけで、元来この場所にひとが来ることは当たり前のことなんですが。
lines.english: Hiyoko was swept along by my urgency. Thinking calmly, we merely happened to have been alone until now. It was perfectly natural for other people to visit this place.

lines.japanese: 「だから、そこの倉庫へ隠れてやり過ごしましょう。俺まだ、日和子さんとたくさん話したいっすもん」
lines.english: “So let’s hide in that storage shed until they leave. I still have so much I want to talk about with you.”

lines.japanese: 「え、でも……あ、ああっ」
lines.english: “But... Oh!”

lines.japanese: 「失礼しまーす」
lines.english: “Pardon us.”

lines.japanese: 扉を開けると、用具倉庫は予想よりはるかに乱雑としていて、足の踏み場もないほどでした。
lines.english: When I opened the door, I found the equipment shed far more cluttered than expected, without so much as a clear place to stand.

lines.japanese: しかし近付いてくる男子生徒らの話し声が、俺から躊躇を奪いました。日和子さんの手を引き、わずか数百平方センチの窮屈な空間へ飛びこみます。
lines.english: But the approaching voices of male students stripped away my hesitation. Pulling Hiyoko by the hand, I jumped into a cramped space of only a few hundred square centimeters.

lines.japanese: 「寒っ！　うわ、無理無理。こんな中やるの絶対無理」
lines.english: “It’s freezing! No way, no way. We can’t do anything out here.”

lines.japanese: 「マジで？　せっかくボール持ってきたのに」
lines.english: “Seriously? And I brought the ball all this way.”

lines.japanese: 「仕方ねー、帰ろうぜ」
lines.english: “Can’t be helped. Let’s go home.”

lines.japanese: ひとの気配がなくなるまで、しばらく息を殺していました。
lines.english: We held our breath for a while, until every sign of their presence was gone.
